questions.question: Who founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sir William Jones**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded on Jan 15, 1784**, by **Sir William Jones**, an Orientalist, to encourage Oriental studies.
 
• An outstanding scholar from the University of Oxford, arrived in Calcutta (now Kolkata) in 1783, as a **supreme court judge**. The society was founded after his arrival.
 
• The Asiatic Society had the** support of Warren Hastings**, the Governor-General (1772–85) of Bengal.
 
• The society owns an** art collection** which includes paintings by Peter Paul Rubens and Joshua Reynolds.
 
• **Indians were first admitted as members of the Asiatic Society in 1829.**
 
• The society’s library contains some 100,000 general volumes, and more than 27,000 books o Sanskrit, manuscripts, prints, coins, and engravings.
 
• The **Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal** is published regularly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• West Bengal is a state in **eastern India**, between the Himalayas and the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Its capital, Kolkata (formerly Calcutta), retains **architectural and cultural remnants **of its past as an East India Company trading post and capital of the British Raj.
 
• Trinamool leader **Mamata Banerjee** is **West Bengal's incumbent chief minister**, the first woman to hold the office.
 
• **Shri C V Anand ** assumed charge of the office of the **Governor of West Bengal** on 18th July 2022.

questions.question: In which town The Supreme Court was established for the First time under the Regulating Act of 1773?

__
 
• **The Supreme Court at Calcutta** was established on 22 October 1774 by the Regulating Act of 1773.
 
• The drawback of this act was that the powers of the SC were not clearly defined.
 
• It replaced the Mayer’s Court of Calcutta.
 
• Sir Elijah Impey was the first judge of this court.
 
• Lemaister was also a Puisne Judge of the Supreme Court of Calcutta.
 
• The Supreme Court was with One Chief Justice and three other judges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Regulating Act of 1773 was an act of the British Government in which government takes step first time to control and regulate the affairs of EIC in India.
 
• It had civil and criminal jurisdiction over the British subjects and not Indian natives.
 
• It has great constitutional importance.
 
• It prohibited the servants of the Company from engaging in any private trade or accepting presents or bribes from the natives.
 
• The Court formed under this act has the following composition:
 
 
• Elijah Impey- CJI. 
 
• Lemaistre- Puisne Judge from 1774 to 1777.
 
• John Hyde- Puisne Judge from 1774 to 1796.
 
• Rober Chambers- Puisne Judge from 1774 to 1783.
 
• Sir William Jones- Puisne judge from 1783 to 1794.

questions.question: When was the Atmiya Sabha founded to attack the evils within Hinduism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1814**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** established the** Atmiya Sabha in 1815 **with **the aim of promoting monotheism and combating regressive practices within Hinduism.**
 
• This philosophical discussion circle served as a platform for debates and discussions on various philosophical topics, while also advocating for social reform.
 
• Roy is hailed as a trailblazer of Hindu reform movements in **19th and 20th century India.**
 
• He vehemently opposed practices such as **child marriage, the caste system, and Sati, advocating** instead for the inheritance rights of daughters and the remarriage rights of widows.
 
• Often referred to as the father of the modern Indian Renaissance, Roy's efforts in the 18th and 19th centuries sparked transformative changes in Indian society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy,** an eminent Indian reformer, played a pivotal role in shaping the **Brahmo Sabha,** **established in 1828**, which later evolved into the **Brahmo Samaj**—a significant social-religious reform movement in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Bestowed with the title of Raja by **Mughal Emperor Akbar II**, Roy wielded considerable influence across various spheres including politics, public administration, education, and religion.
 
• He spearheaded campaigns to eradicate the abhorrent practices of Sati and child marriage, earning him widespread acclaim.
 
• Regarded as the** "Father of Indian Renaissance" **by many historians, Roy's enduring legacy continues to be celebrated, as evidenced by his ranking as the 10th Greatest Bengali of All Time in BBC's 2004 poll.

questions.question: How many members (elected and nominated) were there in the Council of State under the Government of India Act 1919 passed by the Parliament of the United Kingdom to expand participation of Indians in the government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__60.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Government of India Act 1919 **, established the **Council of State as the upper house of bicameral legislature in India.**
 
• Th**e Council of State had 60 members, 34 elected and 26 nominated member**s, with **tenure of five years.**
 
• The GOI Act 1919 was based on the **recommendations of Edwin Montagu**, the Secretary of State for India and **Lord Chelmsford**, the Viceroy of India.
 
• So, GOI Act 1919 also known as** Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****GOI Act 1919, Important Facts:**

 
• **Diarchy**:

 
 
• Introduced diarchy in provinces with divided subjects (Transferred to Indian ministers, Reserved under British control).
 
 
 
• **Bicameral Legislature**:
 
 
• Established two houses at the Centre: Council of State (Upper House) and Legislative Assembly (Lower House).
 
 
 
• **Expanded Provincial Councils**:
 
 
• Increased the number of elected Indian members in provincial councils.
 
 
 
• **Limited Franchise**:
 
 
• Expanded, but limited suffrage based on property and educational qualifications.
 
• Voting rights extended to some women under restrictive conditions.
 
 
 
• **Separate Electorates**:
 
 
• Continued separate electorates for Muslims, Sikhs, and Anglo-Indians.
 
 
 
• **Clear Division**:
 
 
• Demarcation of Central and Provincial subjects.
 
• Provincial subjects split into Transferred and Reserved categories.
 
 
 
• **Governor-General Powers**:
 
 
• Governor-General retained overriding authority over legislative decisions.
 
 
 
• **Public Service Commission**:
 
 
• Introduced the establishment of a Public Service Commission for recruitment.
 
 
 
• **Step Towards Reform**:
 
 
• ​Aimed as a step towards responsible governmenrt, precursor to the 1935 Act.

questions.question: Which of the following was established by Jyotirao Govindrao Phule in 1873 to fight against idolatry and caste system?

options.text: Shree Narayan Guru Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Movement

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Satyashodhak Samaj.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj:-**

 
 
• It was a social reform society founded by Jyotiba Phule in Pune, Maharashtra, on 24 September 1873.
 
• **The society's primary goal was to promote education and social rights for the deprived groups of the society, including the Shudras and Atishudras (the lower castes).**
 
• The Satyashodhak Samaj's main objectives were to:
 
 
• **Challenge the caste system and Brahmanical supremacy**
 
• **Promote education for the Shudras and Atishudras**
 
• **Improve the status of women**
 
• **Promote social reform and social justice **
 
 
 
• The Satyashodhak Samaj was a major force for social change in Maharashtra.
 
• It helped to raise awareness of the plight of the Shudras and Atishudras and to challenge the caste system.
 
• The society also helped to promote education for women and to improve their status in society.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Shree Narayana Dharma Paripalana:-**

 
 
• SNDP Movement was a social reform movement founded by Sree Narayana Guru, a Hindu saint and social reformer from Kerala, India.
 
• The movement was founded in 1903 with the goal of uplifting the Ezhava community, a Hindu caste that was historically marginalized and discriminated against.
 
 
 
• **Young Bengal Movement:-**
 
 
• It was an intellectual movement that emerged in the early 19th century among Bengali students at Hindu College in Calcutta, India.
 
• The movement was influenced by Western Enlightenment ideas and challenged traditional Hindu beliefs and practices.
 
• The Young Bengal leaders, also known as Derozians, after their teacher Henry Louis Vivian Derozio, were known for their radical and rationalist thinking.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj:-**
 
 
• It was a Hindu reform movement founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 in Bombay, India.
 
• The movement aimed to revitalize Hinduism by returning to its Vedic roots and purging it of later accretions and superstitions.
 
• The Arya Samaj emphasized the monotheistic worship of a single God, the authority of the Vedas, and the importance of education and social reform.

• It was **responsible for administering the British legal system** in India.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ** Regulating Act of 1773****​**

 
 
• The 'Regulating Act' of 1773 was passed by the British Parliament to control the territories of the East India Company majorly in Bengal.
 
• This act was passed due to the misgovernment by the British East India government that introduced a situation of bankruptcy and the government had to interfere with the affairs of the Company.
 
• The Regulating Act was passed in the British Parliament in June 1773.

questions.question: Satyashodhak Samaj (truth seeker society) was established by which of the following social reformers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotiba Phule**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jyotiba Phule** established the Satyashodhak Samaj (truth seeker society) in 1873.
 
• The primary objective of the Satyashodhak Samaj was to liberate the oppressed classes from the exploitation and atrocities of the upper caste Brahmins.
 
• Jyotiba Phule was a prominent social reformer and activist who worked for the upliftment of the marginalized communities in India.
 
• The movement aimed to promote social equality and remove caste-based discrimination.
 
• Satyashodhak Samaj also focused on education and the emancipation of women, emphasizing the importance of education for all sections of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jyotiba Phule** is also known for his efforts in the field of education, having established the first girls' school in Pune in 1848.
 
• He, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, worked tirelessly towards the education and upliftment of women and the lower castes.
 
• Jyotiba Phule authored several books and plays that highlighted social issues and called for reforms.
 
• His notable works include "Gulamgiri" and "Shetkarayacha Asud," which criticized the caste system and the exploitation of farmers.
 
• Jyotiba Phule's contributions have had a lasting impact on the social fabric of India, and he is remembered as a pioneer in the fight against social injustice.

questions.question: Who succeeded Alivardi Khan as Nawab of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Siraj-ud-Daulah**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Siraj-ud-Daulah **succeeded **Alivardi Khan **as the Nawab of Bengal after Alivardi Khan's death in **1756**. 
 
• He was **Alivardi Khan's grandson** and the **last independent Nawab of Bengal **before British rule. 
 
• Siraj-ud-Daulah is most noted for his role in the Battle of Plassey in 1757, where he faced the British East India Company.
 
• The defeat at Plassey, largely due to betrayal by his commander Mir Jafar, led to** British dominance in India**, marking a significant shift in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alivardi Khan**__

 __
 
• He was the Nawab of Bengal from **1740 to 1756**.
 
• He toppled the Nasiri dynasty of Nawabs and assumed power himself.
 
• He is also known for his victory during the **Battle of Burdwan** against the Maratha Empire during the Maratha invasions of Bengal.​
 
 
 
• **Mir Jaffar & Mir Kasim**__
 
 
• British East India Company made** Mir Jafar** the first dependent Nawab of Bengal under them.
 
• **Mir Jafar was a successor of Siraj ud-Daulah** to whom he served as a Commander and betrayed him in the Battle of Plassey.
 
• **Mir Qasim** was the Nawab of Bengal from 1760 to 1763.
 
• He was installed as Nawab with the support of the British East India Company, **replacing Mir Jafar**, his father-in-law, who had himself been supported earlier by the East India Company after his role in winning the Battle of Plassey for the British.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts, enacted by the British Parliament, provided for the establishment of a Law Commission for the consolidation and codification of Indian Laws?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act, 1833**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Charter Act of 1833** marked a significant milestone in Indian legal history by **instituting a Law Commission** tasked **with the consolidation and codification of Indian laws.**
 
• Established in 1834, the inaugural Law Commission was helmed by TB Macaulay.
 
• Under Macaulay's leadership, the commission's recommendations paved the way for the formalization of the Criminal Procedure Code and the penal code, laying the groundwork for a more organized legal framework in India.
 
• Furthermore, the Charter Act of 1833 heralded a pivotal shift in India's administrative landscape by opening up avenues for Indian participation.
 
• It mandated that government employment be allocated based on merit rather than factors such as race, religion, color, or birth, signaling a move towards a more inclusive and equitable governance structure.
 
• Subsequently, the Charter Act of 1853 saw the establishment of the second Law Commission in England, commencing its operations in the same year. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Indian Councils Act of 1909,** passed by the British Parliament, initiated some reforms in the legislative councils and partially expanded Indian involvement in the governance of British India.
 
• **The Government of India (GOI) Act of 1919 **marked a significant step by the administration towards the eventual introduction of responsible government in India, marking a pivotal moment in its governance.
 
• **The Charter Act of 1813,** also referred to as the East India Company Act of 1813, was legislation enacted by the British Parliament to renew the charter of the British East India Company for an additional 20 years.

questions.question: Which amongst the following statements about the Indian social reformers of the 19th century is INCORRECT?

options.text: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj.
The Aligarh Movement was started by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan in 1875.
Mahadev Govind Ranade is associated with the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha
Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** was not the founder of the Brahmo Samaj. The Brahmo Samaj was founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in 1828.
 
• The **Aligarh Movement** was indeed started by **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** in 1875 to promote modern education among Muslims.
 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade** is correctly associated with the **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha**, an organization aimed at promoting social and political reforms.
 
• **Dayanand Saraswati** founded the **Arya Samaj** in 1875, advocating for a return to the teachings of the Vedas and promoting social reform.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** was a prominent social reformer known for his efforts in promoting education and widow remarriage.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj played a crucial role in modernizing Indian society and promoting rational thinking and social reforms.
 
• The **Aligarh Movement** led to the establishment of the **Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College**, which later became the **Aligarh Muslim University**.
 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade** was also a judge and one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The **Arya Samaj** had a significant influence on Indian society, promoting values such as equality, social justice, and the importance of education.

questions.question: Who among the following was NOT associated with ‘Prarthana Sabha’?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **Motilal Nehru.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Prarthana Sabha:**

__
 
• The **Prarthana Sabha **was founded in 1867 in Bombay by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang.
 
• It was an off-shoot of** Brahmo Samaj.**
 
• It was a reform movement within Hinduism and Justice **M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar **joined it in 1870 and infused new strength to it.
 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade also ran the Deccan Education Society.**
 
• Several members of the **Prarthana Sabha** had earlier been active in the Paramhansa Mandali.
 
• This Sabha denounced idolatry, priestly domination, caste rigidities, and preferred monotheism.
 
• It also concentrated on **social reforms like inter-dining, inter-marriage, widow remarriage, and the uplift of women and depressed classes.**
 
• Apart from Hindu sects, it also drew upon Christianity and Buddhism.
 
• It sought truth in all religions.
 
• Drawing inspiration from the **Maratha Bhakti saints** of the medieval period, Ranade sought to establish the concept of one compassionate God.
 
• **Veeresalingam Pantulu** was the Telugu reformer who encouraged the **Prarthana Sabha in South India.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade (1842-1901)**

 
 
• He was an Indian nationalist, social reformer, scholar, and jurist. Known as the "Socrates of Maharashtra," he advocated social, religious, and political reforms.
 
• Ranade co-founded the Deccan Educational Society, supported the Indian National Congress, and promoted Hindu-Muslim unity.
 
 
 
• **Atmaram Pandurang - **
 
 
• He was an Indian physician and social reformer.
 
• He founded the Prarthana Samaj. He was one of the two Indian co-founders of the Bombay Natural History Society.
 
• He also served as Sheriff of Bombay.
 
 
 
• **RG Bhandarkar -**
 
 
• In 1853, while a student, Bhandarkar became a member of the Paramhansa Sabha, an association for furthering liberal ideas which was then secret to avoid the wrath of the powerful and orthodox elements of contemporary society.
 
• Visits from Keshub Chandra Sen during 1864 had inspired the members of the Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Motilal Nehru -**
 
 
• He was eloquent speaker, a noted Parliamentarian and a prominent figure of the Indian nationalism in the Gandhian era, was born on 6 May 1861 at Agra.
 
• His forefathers hailed from Kashmir, but had settled in Delhi since the beginning of the eighteenth century.
 
• Motilal Nehru spent his childhood at Khetri in Rajasthan.

questions.question: The Arya Samaj was founded in ______ by Swami Dayanand Saraswati.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1875__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Arya Samaj** was founded in **1875 **by **Swami Dayanand Saraswati.**
 
• It was a **Hindu socio-religious** and **reform organization**.
 
• Monotheism and the Infallible authority of the Vedas are the 2 most basic tenets of Arya Samaj.
 
• Arya Samaj worked in spreading Hinduism through the study of Vedas and Upanishads and converting non-Hindus through the Shuddhi movement.
 
• It also worked against social evils like child marriage, untouchability, the caste system, and gender inequality.
 
• It founded the Dayanand Anglo Vedic (DAV) Colleges to revive the ancient Indian Gurukul system. The first DAV College was established in Lahore in 1886.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** __**Dayanand Saraswati**__

 
• Dayanand Saraswati was born on **12 Feb 1824** in **Kathiawad, Gujarat**. His real name was **Mool Shankar Tiwari**.
 
• Also known as **Maharishi Dayanand**, he was a **Vedanta scholar of Hinduism** and also a social reformer who **denounced idolatry and ritualistic worship**.
 
• His most famous work is **Satyarth Prakash**.
 
• He died on** 30 Oct 1883.**

• Providing education, healthcare, and disaster relief.
 
• Engaging in various social welfare activities, such as running schools, hospitals, and orphanages.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Faraizi Movement** was founded by **Haji Shariatullah** in the early 19th century. The movement aimed at purifying Islam by eliminating un-Islamic practices among Bengali Muslims. Hence, A matches with 4.
 
• **Mohammedan Literary Society** was established by **Nawab Abdul Latif** in 1863 in Kolkata. The society aimed at promoting modern education among Muslims. Hence, B matches with 3.
 
• **Indian Patriotic Association** was founded by **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** in 1888. It aimed at creating loyalty among Indians towards the British government and countering the Congress Party. Hence, C matches with 2.
 
• **Wahabi Movement** was led by **Sayyid Ahmad of Rae Bareli** in India. This movement aimed at purging Islam of any un-Islamic practices and restoring it to its original form. Hence, D matches with 1.

 __
 
• It focused on religious reforms and aimed to remove innovations (bid'ah) and practices considered un-Islamic.
 
• The movement was significant in mobilizing the Bengali Muslim peasantry.
 
 
 
• **Mohammedan Literary Society:**__
 __
 
• It played a crucial role in the social and educational upliftment of Muslims in Bengal.
 
• The society also promoted the use of the English language among Indian Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Indian Patriotic Association:**__
 __
 
• It was an important political organization during the British Raj, advocating for loyalty to the British crown.
 
• The association also worked to counter the influence of the Indian National Congress.
 
 
 
• **Wahabi Movement:**__
 
 
• It was part of the larger Islamic revivalist movement that originated in Arabia.
 
• The movement had a significant impact on the religious and political landscape of India during the 19th century.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Vice President of the Interim Government formed by Congress in 1946?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** served as the **Vice President of the Interim Government** established by the **Congress in 1946**.
 
• This interim administration came into existence on September 2, 1946, and comprised members selected from the newly elected Constituent Assembly.
 
• The **Congress Party secured 208 seats **in the assembly, while the Muslim League won 73 seats.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru, as the Vice President of the Council, wielded powers akin to those of a Prime Minister.
 
• This interim arrangement persisted until **August 15, 1947**, when India and Pakistan gained independence from colonial rule.
 
• During this period, **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** was appointed to lead the Department of Education. Additionally, with the inclusion of the Muslim League in the Interim Government, the Department of Finance was helmed by Liaquat Ali Khan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Viceroy's Executive Council **underwent a transformation to become the executive branch of the interim government.
 
• Initially overseen by the **Viceroy of India**, it was restructured into a council of ministers, with the **Vice-President of the Council, Jawaharlal Nehru,** assuming the powers akin to those of a Prime Minister.
 
• Following independence, all members of this council would be Indians, except for the Viceroy, who in August transitioned to the role of Governor-General.
 
• **Lord Mountbatten** would hold a ceremonial position, while the Commander-in-Chief, India, initially Sir Claude Auchinleck, was succeeded after independence by General Sir Rob Lockhart.
 
• Vallabhbhai Patel, a prominent Congress leader, occupied the second-most powerful position within the Council. He was entrusted with heading the Department of Home Affairs and the Department of Information and Broadcasting.

questions.question: During the British rule in India, which of the following Governor Generals devised the ‘Doctrine of Lapse’, a policy of annexation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Dalhousie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Dalhousie**, Governor-General of the English East India Company from **1848 to 1856,** instituted the **Doctrine of Lapse,** an annexation strategy across the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Under this policy, the Company would **absorb territories** under the subsidiary alliance if the ruling authority failed to leave a natural heir.
 
• This facilitated the Company's acquisition of regions governed by rulers without successors.
 
• The Doctrine remained in effect until 1858, following the transition from Company rule to the British Raj under direct Crown administration.
 
• **Elements of the Doctrine **persisted in Indian governance, used to discontinue recognition of individual princely families until 1971, when the Indira Gandhi administration ceased acknowledgment of former ruling dynasties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **James Andrew Broun-Ramsay, **1st Marquess of Dalhousie, previously known as the **Earl of Dalhousie** from **1838 to 1849, **was a prominent Scottish statesman and colonial administrator during the British Raj in India.
 
• Serving as **Governor-General from 1848 to 1856**, he left a lasting legacy on the Indian subcontinent. His contributions to the colonial educational system were significant, as he expanded its scope to include mass education alongside elite higher education.
 
• Dalhousie's reforms extended beyond education; he introduced passenger trains to the railway network, implemented the electric telegraph system, and standardized postage rates, labeling them as the "three great engines of social improvement."
 
• Additionally, he established the **Public Works Department** in India. Dalhousie's tenure as Governor-General is characterized by his forward-thinking approach, which consolidated East India Company rule in India and laid the groundwork for subsequent administrations.
 
• His strategic policies played a crucial role in quelling potential rebellions, providing stability for future governance in the region.
